Introduction_1: This simple, single-skillet meal requires minimal prep and cooks completely on the stovetop. Eggs, chickpeas, and spinach simmer in a spiced tomato sauce for a hearty start to the day.
Ingredient_7_1: 14.5 oz (411 g) No-salt-added canned diced tomatoes, undrained
Ingredient_8_1: 1/2 cup (130 g) No-salt-added canned chickpeas, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_11_1: 1/2 cup (113 g) Nonfat plain Greek yogurt
Ingredient_12_1: 1 large (60 g) Whole-wheat pita bread, halved
Instruction_1_1: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Instruction_2_1: Stir in garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 to 2 minutes.
Instruction_3_1: Pour in vinegar, tomatoes, and chickpeas. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then lower heat to medium-low and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, 4 to 5 minutes.
Instruction_4_1: Stir spinach into the skillet in handfuls. Cook until the leaves are bright green and wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.
Instruction_5_1: Form shallow wells in the hot tomato mixture using a spoon. Crack an egg into each well.
Instruction_6_1: Cover the skillet with a lid and cook over low heat until the egg whites are firm but the yolks remain soft, 4 to 6 minutes.
Instruction_7_1: Remove the skillet from the heat. Divide the warm shakshuka between plates and serve immediately with Greek yogurt and pita bread.
Variation_1: Trade the spinach for chopped curly kale and simmer longer.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.
Introduction_2: For a satisfying breakfast that feels like a weekend treat, these hearty pancakes deliver lasting morning fuel. Whole oats and cottage cheese blend into a protein-rich batter topped with an instant blueberry jam.
Ingredient_3_2: 1 cup (226 g) No-salt-added low-fat cottage cheese
Instruction_1_2: Combine the frozen blueberries and chia seeds in a microwave-safe bowl, then microwave on high for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbling and bursting.
Instruction_2_2: Blend the cottage cheese, oats, eggs, hemp hearts, baking powder, cinnamon, and vanilla extract in a blender on high until the batter is smooth.
Instruction_3_2: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush with the olive oil until shimmering.
Instruction_4_2: Pour the batter into the pan in small circles to form the pancakes.
Instruction_5_2: Cook the pancakes in batches for 4 to 6 minutes per batch, flipping halfway through when the edges appear set and the bottoms are golden brown.
Instruction_6_2: Transfer the finished pancakes to a plate and repeat until all the batter is used.
Instruction_7_2: Divide the warm pancakes between plates and spoon the thickened blueberry-chia jam over the top.
Variation_2: Swap the frozen blueberries for frozen dark sweet cherries.
Storage_2: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat pancakes in a dry skillet.

Title_1: Creamy Mixed Berry and Almond Smoothie Bowls
Introduction_1: This simple no-cook breakfast requires only a quick blitz in the blender. Silken tofu, frozen berries, and creamy almond butter combine into a remarkably thick base that keeps hunger away until lunch.
Ingredient_4_1: 1 medium (118 g) Banana, peeled and broken into pieces
Instruction_1_1: Place the drained silken tofu, unsweetened soy milk, frozen mixed berries, banana, creamy almond butter, chia seeds, rolled oats, and cinnamon into a high-speed blender.
Instruction_2_1: Blend on low speed to incorporate the dry and frozen ingredients into the liquids.
Instruction_3_1: Increase the speed to high and blend until completely smooth and remarkably thick, stopping once or twice to scrape down the sides or use a blender tamper as needed.
Instruction_4_1: Divide the thick mixture evenly between two bowls and serve immediately.
Variation_1: Swap the creamy almond butter for unsweetened natural peanut butter.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.
Title_2: Fluffy Egg White Oatmeal with Berries and Walnuts
Introduction_2: This simple stovetop technique transforms ordinary oats into a creamy, filling morning meal. Simmering rolled oats with liquid egg whites creates a thick bowl without relying on protein powders.
Instruction_1_2: Combine the water, almond milk, oats, cinnamon, and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.
Instruction_2_2: Reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook the oats for 5 to 7 minutes, checking at 5 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the oats are tender.
Instruction_3_2: Pour the liquid egg whites into the simmering oats in a slow stream while stirring vigorously to prevent scrambling.
Instruction_4_2: Cook and stir the mixture for 2 to 3 minutes, checking at 2 minutes, until it becomes thick and the egg whites are opaque.
Instruction_5_2: Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in the frozen berries and vanilla extract so the residual heat thaws the fruit.
Instruction_6_2: Divide the warm oatmeal between two bowls. Top with the chopped walnuts before serving.
Variation_2: Swap the chopped walnuts for sliced almonds or toasted pecans.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.

Title_1: Lemony Sardine and Avocado Whole-Grain Toast
Introduction_1: Start the day with a substantial hit of lean protein and fiber for steady energy and lasting fullness.
Ingredient_1_1: 4 slices (136 g) Low-sodium sprouted whole-grain bread, toasted
Ingredient_2_1: 3.5 oz (100 g) Avocado, pitted and peeled
Ingredient_4_1: 1 tsp (2 g) Fresh lemon zest, finely grated
Ingredient_7_1: 2 cans (212 g) No-salt-added canned sardines in water, drained
Ingredient_8_1: 1/4 tsp (1 g) Crushed red pepper flakes
Ingredient_9_1: 5 oz (150 g) Fresh strawberries, hulled and halved
Instruction_1_1: Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Instruction_2_1: Mash the avocado in a bowl with the lemon juice and lemon zest until combined but slightly chunky.
Instruction_3_1: Spread the mashed avocado evenly across the toast slices.
Instruction_4_1: Layer the baby arugula and halved cherry tomatoes over the avocado.
Instruction_5_1: Break the drained sardines into large pieces with a fork and arrange them on top of the vegetables.
Instruction_6_1: Sprinkle the crushed red pepper flakes evenly over the toasts.
Instruction_7_1: Serve immediately with the fresh strawberries on the side.
Variation_1: Trade the baby arugula for fresh baby spinach leaves.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; assembled toast does not keep.
Title_2: Mediterranean Salmon and Hummus Breakfast Wraps
Introduction_2: This fast, no-cook breakfast is ready to eat as quickly as you can mix and assemble the ingredients. Flaky canned salmon and creamy hummus replace traditional breakfast meats to create a morning wrap that prevents mid-morning hunger.
Ingredient_2_2: 8.5 oz (240 g) Canned pink salmon (no-salt-added), rinsed and drained, flaked
Ingredient_9_2: 1/4 cup (40 g) Red onion, thinly sliced
Instruction_1_2: Flake the salmon with a fork in a medium bowl.
Instruction_2_2: Stir the hummus, lemon juice, dill, and black pepper into the salmon until combined.
Instruction_3_2: Lay the whole-wheat tortillas flat on a clean workspace and distribute the baby spinach evenly over each.
Instruction_4_2: Spoon the salmon and hummus mixture evenly over the spinach.
Instruction_5_2: Top with the diced cucumber and sliced red onion.
Instruction_6_2: Roll the tortillas tightly to form firm wraps.
Instruction_7_2: Serve the wraps immediately with the fresh berries on the side.
Variation_2: Swap the baby spinach for fresh arugula or baby kale.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep well once assembled.

Title_1: Minty Smashed Green Pea and Egg Toasts
Introduction_1: Cool mint and a creamy yogurt-pea mash top crisp whole-grain toast in this savory, satisfying breakfast.
Ingredient_2_1: 1/3 cup (75 g) Nonfat plain Greek yogurt
Ingredient_4_1: 2 tbsp (3 g) Fresh mint, finely chopped
Instruction_1_1: Boil water in a small pot over high heat. Add the peas, cook for 2 to 3 minutes until tender, and drain well.
Instruction_2_1: Transfer the warm peas to a bowl. Add the yogurt, lemon juice, mint, and garlic powder, mashing with a fork until chunky but spreadable.
Instruction_3_1: Whisk the whole eggs and egg whites together in a small bowl until fully blended.
Instruction_4_1: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Pour in the eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring gently until soft curds form.
Instruction_6_1: Spread the minted pea mash evenly over the warm toasts. Top with the scrambled eggs and crumbled feta.
Instruction_7_1: Serve immediately alongside the sliced fresh strawberries.
Variation_1: Swap the fresh mint for fresh dill or chopped basil.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; assembled toasts do not keep.
Title_2: Open-Faced Tomato and Spinach Egg Melts
Introduction_2: This energizing breakfast transforms a heavy morning sandwich into a satisfying open-faced meal. A mix of eggs piled over whole wheat muffins with fresh tomato, mozzarella, and a side of strawberries keeps you full until lunch.
Ingredient_1_2: 2 (114 g) 100% whole wheat English muffins, split
Ingredient_8_2: 1 oz (28 g) Part-skim mozzarella cheese slices, halved
Ingredient_9_2: 3 cups (430 g) Fresh strawberries, hulled and halved
Instruction_1_2: Toast the English muffin halves until golden and crisp.
Instruction_2_2: Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted.
Instruction_3_2: Whisk the whole eggs, liquid egg whites, and black pepper in a small bowl. Pour into the skillet with the spinach and scramble for 2 to 3 minutes until mostly set.
Instruction_4_2: Lay the tomato slices and halved mozzarella cheese slices directly over the eggs. Cover the skillet, remove from the heat, and let sit for 1 minute until the cheese melts.
Instruction_5_2: Divide the egg and tomato scramble over the open-faced muffin halves.
Instruction_6_2: Serve immediately with the fresh strawberries on the side.
Variation_2: Swap the strawberries for two cups of sliced fresh peaches.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.

Title_1: Pinto Bean and Avocado Breakfast Tostadas
Introduction_1: Eating a combination of plant and egg protein in the morning helps maintain steady energy and lasting fullness until lunch.
Ingredient_4_1: 1 1/2 cups (255 g) No-salt-added canned pinto beans, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_9_1: 1/2 cup (110 g) Fresh pico de gallo
Instruction_1_1: Place a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the raw pepitas and toast for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and fragrant, then transfer to a small bowl.
Instruction_2_1: Warm the corn tortillas in the same skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until pliable and lightly toasted. Transfer to serving plates.
Instruction_3_1: Add the extra-virgin olive oil, drained pinto beans, and ground cumin to the skillet over medium heat. Mash the beans roughly using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula for 3 to 4 minutes until warmed through, then divide evenly over the tortillas.
Instruction_4_1: Add the baby spinach to the skillet and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted. Layer the spinach evenly over the mashed beans.
Instruction_5_1: Whisk the whole eggs and egg whites together in a bowl. Pour into the skillet over medium-low heat and stir gently with a silicone spatula for 2 to 3 minutes until soft curds form and the eggs are set.
Instruction_6_1: Spoon the scrambled eggs over the spinach. Top the tostadas evenly with the fresh pico de gallo, sliced avocado, and the toasted pepitas.
Variation_1: Swap the baby spinach for thinly sliced fresh Tuscan kale.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep well once assembled.
Title_2: Savory Farro Breakfast Bowls with Eggs and Spinach
Introduction_2: Starting your morning with intact grains and lean protein provides steady energy and lasting fullness. This single-skillet meal uses a convenient cooked grain pouch to keep prep time minimal.
Ingredient_9_2: 1/4 tsp (0.5 g) Crushed red pepper flakes
Instruction_1_2: Whisk the whole eggs and liquid egg whites together in a small bowl.
Instruction_2_2: Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they blister and soften, checking at 3 minutes.
Instruction_3_2: Break up the farro in its pouch, then add it to the skillet along with the spinach. Stir and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach wilts and the farro is warmed through.
Instruction_4_2: Push the farro and vegetable mixture to the outer edges of the skillet to create an empty space in the center. Pour the egg mixture directly into the open space.
Instruction_5_2: Cook the eggs for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring the center frequently with a spatula until softly scrambled and just set, checking at 3 minutes.
Instruction_6_2: Remove the skillet from the heat. Fold the scrambled eggs into the farro mixture, then stir in the salt, black pepper, crushed red pepper flakes, and lemon juice.
Instruction_7_2: Divide the mixture into serving bowls and sprinkle with the hemp hearts before serving.
Variation_2: Swap the fresh baby spinach for chopped Tuscan kale.
Storage_2: Keeps up to 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently in microwave.

Introduction_1: Starting your morning with a generous serving of lean protein and fiber helps maintain steady energy right through to lunch. This fresh, zero-cook bowl relies on artichokes and whole-wheat pita to deliver lasting fullness without weighing you down.
Ingredient_1_1: 1 1/2 cups (340 g) Nonfat plain Greek yogurt
Ingredient_5_1: 8 oz (225 g) Low-sodium canned artichoke hearts, rinsed, drained, and quartered
Ingredient_7_1: 2 tbsp (18 g) Kalamata olives, pitted and minced
Instruction_1_1: Whisk the Greek yogurt and lemon juice together in a small bowl until completely smooth.
Instruction_2_1: Spread the yogurt mixture evenly across the bottoms of two wide, shallow bowls.
Instruction_3_1: Arrange the chopped cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and quartered artichoke hearts generously over the yogurt.
Instruction_4_1: Drizzle the extra-virgin olive oil over the vegetables, then scatter the minced olives, pumpkin seeds, and dried oregano on top.
Instruction_5_1: Toast the whole-wheat pitas in a toaster until slightly crisp and warm, then cut them into wedges.
Instruction_6_1: Serve the bowls immediately with the warm pita wedges on the side for scooping.
Variation_1: Swap the whole-wheat pita for a side of cooked quinoa.
Storage_1: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; toast the pita just before serving.
Title_2: Smoky Tomato Navy Beans and Eggs on Toast
Introduction_2: Start your morning with this satisfying, single-pan savory skillet. It reimagines sugary baked beans as a fast, high-fiber dish that provides steady energy until lunch.
Ingredient_6_2: 9 oz (260 g) No-salt-added canned navy beans, rinsed and drained
Instruction_1_2: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Toast the whole-wheat bread in a toaster.
Instruction_2_2: Add the tomato paste, smoked paprika, and garlic powder to the skillet. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Instruction_3_2: Stir in the drained navy beans, water, apple cider vinegar, salt, and baby spinach. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until the spinach wilts and the liquid forms a thick sauce.
Instruction_4_2: Push the bean mixture aside to create wide wells in the skillet. Crack the eggs into the wells.
Instruction_5_2: Cover the skillet and cook for 4 to 6 minutes. Check at 4 minutes to ensure the egg whites are completely set and the yolks remain soft.
Instruction_6_2: Divide the toasted bread between plates. Scoop the eggs and smoky beans over the top to serve.
Variation_2: Swap the navy beans for no-salt-added canned cannellini beans.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; cooked eggs and toast do not keep.

Title_1: Smoky White Bean and Broccoli Skillet Frittata
Introduction_1: This simple skillet breakfast requires minimal prep and moves quickly from the stovetop to the oven. Folding white beans into a mix of eggs and broccoli creates a filling base that pairs well with fresh oranges.
Ingredient_4_1: 9 oz (260 g) No-salt-added canned navy beans, rinsed and drained
Ingredient_9_1: 1/2 oz (14 g) Sharp cheddar cheese, shredded
Ingredient_10_1: 2 medium (260 g) Fresh oranges, peeled and segmented
Instruction_1_1: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Whisk the whole eggs, liquid egg whites, smoked paprika, and black pepper in a medium bowl until combined.
Instruction_2_1: Heat the olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Instruction_3_1: Add the red onion to the skillet and cook until softened, 3 to 4 minutes, checking at 3 minutes.
Instruction_4_1: Stir in the frozen broccoli and drained navy beans. Cook until warmed through, 2 to 3 minutes, checking at 2 minutes.
Instruction_5_1: Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables in the skillet. Cook undisturbed on medium-low heat until the edges begin to set, 3 to 4 minutes, checking at 3 minutes.
Instruction_6_1: Sprinkle the cheddar cheese over the top and transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake until the center sets, 5 to 7 minutes, checking at 5 minutes.
Instruction_7_1: Remove the skillet from the oven using an oven mitt. Slice the frittata in half and serve warm with the fresh orange segments.
Variation_1: Swap the cheddar cheese for crumbled feta or goat cheese.
Storage_1: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat briefly in the microwave.
Title_2: Southwestern Tempeh and Pepper Breakfast Scramble
Introduction_2: This energizing breakfast replaces eggs with hearty crumbled tempeh to keep you full well past mid-morning. Smoky cumin and paprika bring bold Southwestern flavor to the skillet without relying on heavy sauces.
Ingredient_2_2: 6 oz (170 g) Frozen bell pepper and onion blend
Instruction_1_2: Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Instruction_2_2: Add the frozen pepper and onion blend. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and any ice has evaporated.
Instruction_3_2: Stir in the crumbled tempeh, ground cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the tempeh is browned and aromatic.
Instruction_4_2: Fold in the halved cherry tomatoes. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until they begin to soften.
Instruction_5_2: Warm the whole-wheat tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave until pliable.
Instruction_6_2: Divide the tempeh scramble between plates. Top with the diced avocado and chopped cilantro, and serve alongside the warm tortillas.
Variation_2: Swap the cherry tomatoes for a handful of baby spinach.
Storage_2: Keeps 2-3 days refrigerated; reheat in a skillet over medium.

Title_1: Tex-Mex Sweet Potato and Black Bean Breakfast Scramble
Introduction_1: Smoky cumin and vibrant salsa deliver bold southwestern flavor to this protein-packed, vegetable-forward breakfast. Pairing convenient frozen sweet potatoes with pantry black beans creates a hearty, high-fiber foundation that helps prevent mid-morning energy crashes.
Ingredient_2_1: 7 oz (200 g) Frozen diced sweet potatoes
Ingredient_4_1: 1 cup (260 g) No-salt-added canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Instruction_1_1: Whisk the liquid egg whites and whole eggs together in a bowl until uniformly smooth.
Instruction_2_1: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat with the olive oil until the oil shimmers.
Instruction_3_1: Add the sweet potatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and browned at the edges, 6 to 8 minutes. Check at 6 minutes.
Instruction_4_1: Reduce the burner to medium. Stir the cumin and black beans into the skillet, tossing gently until the beans are warmed through.
Instruction_5_1: Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables. Cook gently, pushing the eggs across the bottom with a silicone spatula as they begin to set, until fully cooked but still soft, 3 to 4 minutes. Check at 3 minutes.
Instruction_6_1: Remove the skillet from the heat.
Instruction_7_1: Divide the scramble between two plates and top evenly with the salsa, avocado, and cilantro before serving.
Variation_1: Swap the black beans for rinsed, no-salt-added pinto beans.
Storage_1: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.
Title_2: Warm Blueberry and Vanilla Skyr Waffles
Introduction_2: Packing plenty of protein and fiber, this comforting breakfast helps keep your morning energy steady until lunch. Tangy Skyr and warm berries replace sugary syrup for a naturally sweet start.
Instruction_1_2: Toast the whole-wheat waffles in a toaster or oven according to the package directions until golden and crisp.
Instruction_2_2: Place the frozen blueberries in a small saucepan over medium heat while the waffles toast.
Instruction_3_2: Cook the blueberries, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes until the berries soften and burst. Remove the saucepan from the heat.
Instruction_4_2: Whisk the Skyr, vanilla extract, and ground cinnamon in a medium bowl until smooth.
Instruction_5_2: Divide the warm toasted waffles between two plates.
Instruction_6_2: Spoon the vanilla Skyr mixture over the waffles, then ladle the warm blueberry sauce on top.
Instruction_7_2: Sprinkle the hemp hearts and chopped walnuts over the waffles before serving.
Variation_2: Swap the chopped walnuts for sliced almonds or toasted pecans.
Storage_2: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.
